title: Reskinning assets with AI
author: Rsloth
selftext:
Game assets can now trivially be "upgraded" with AI, this is a huge unlock for indie game developers and studios with limited resources or artistic ability. Seems like this will be very disruptive for all of the asset stores as well. As AI tools improve there will be no need to buy overpriced asset packs from a store, you can generate them consistently for pennies.

We're entering the abundance economy. Assets will be 100x cheaper, more time to invest in the game mechanics and experience and less on the grind.

comments.author: florodude
comments.body: "overpriced asset packs". Bet you that if you multiplied all the (Price\*total sales)/(Hours the person worked on it) you'd get less than minimum wage for 99% of these asset packs. This is the shit that people hate our communities for.

replies.author: Rsloth
replies.body: Could it be that the asset stores are the problem charging 20-30% or more per transaction?

replies.author: GreatBigJerk
replies.body:
It's kind of both. 


There are ways to buy assets from storefronts that aren't horrible, but a lot of the popular ones take a huge cut. 


That said, people put a lot of work into asset packs, and using AI to circumvent them does feel shitty. It's basically punching down instead of replacing the bigger companies who regularly screw people over.

replies.author: Embarrassed_Split236
replies.body:
Idk you would think asset packs would be a lot more profitable considering you’re getting high quality art at a fraction of the price. I think the main roadblock is that (much like ai) asset packs vary in art style too much to be easily used for a whole game.

My ideal world would be human assets working alongside ai, letting devs reskin and tweak the packs to fit their game while the rights still belong to the original artist. AI is way better with references, so I’m hoping there will always be a place for cheap assets to be used
